findings.text: follow-on: the discover_status path view still imports get_discovery_threshold and passes it to get_high_value_paths (imas_codex/discovery/paths/frontier.py:1467), a path gate, so §14's section done-when 'every path-gating default reads get_path_scan_threshold()' holds inside imas_codex/discovery/paths but not at this call site; the new guard scans only imas_codex/discovery/paths/*.py so a re-introduction here would not be caught. The §14 node-2 comment assigns this call site to the map session's runner node, so it is out of this node's scope.

follow-on: TriagedDirectory.description is annotated `str` but the triager now passes None when a description is unobserved (scorer.py:391), so to_graph_dict() emits a null description and the annotation misdescribes runtime; the dataclass does not validate, so this is a stale type rather than a crash.

follow-on: the replay test asserts a Jev judgment and the description value but not that a failed describe left the batch's cost/statistics unset; the swallowed exception at scorer.py:385 is measured only by the two parametrised arms, so a regression that also recorded a nonzero description_cost on failure would pass this test.

item_verdicts.diff: read dac0f8f4 against its parent e7464580 in full — scorer.py +45/-26 replaces the direct acall_llm_structured call with describe_paths under a try/except and preserves null descriptions in build_path_judgment_state, plus a 58-line replay test, a 32-line threshold guard and a one-line assertion relaxation.
item_verdicts.done_when: the node-2 done-when names three checks; tests/discovery/test_path_description.py::test_triage_judges_when_description_is_path_keyed_or_fails[path-keyed] and [failed] reach a Jev judgment (manifest after_suite, head-arm-verified.log 82 passed EXIT=0), tests/discovery/test_path_scan_threshold.py fails if any imas_codex/discovery/paths module reads get_discovery_threshold, and live-eddb-triage.log records a stored Jev judgment for /analysis/src/eddb.
item_verdicts.goal: the §14 node-2 scope is to give the describe-then-judge step one caller-shared owner and make a description failure non-blocking, judging the path with its description recorded as unobserved; imas_codex/discovery/paths/scorer.py:372-392 now imports describe_paths and judges with descriptions.get(row["path"]) so a failed describe yields description=None rather than aborting the batch.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records commits dac0f8f4, baseline_suite base-arm-verified.log 10 passed EXIT=0 at e7464580, after_suite head-arm-verified.log 82 passed EXIT=0 at dac0f8f4, negative_control_log negative-control-mutated.log 2 failed EXIT=1, and the live EDDB run; I re-ran the named files at head (reviewer-head.log 13 passed EXIT=0) and they reconcile.
item_verdicts.write_paths: git show --stat dac0f8f4 lists exactly imas_codex/discovery/paths/scorer.py, tests/discovery/test_path_description.py, tests/discovery/test_path_judgments.py and tests/discovery/test_path_scan_threshold.py, the paths the manifest declares in changed_paths and orientation_write_paths.

justifications.durability: the added assertions are independent of the code under test — test_triage_judges_when_description_is_path_keyed_or_fails compares rows[0]["description"] to a constant from its own description_fails parameter, and reverting scorer.py to the direct call reddens both arms (negative-control-mutated.log 2 failed EXIT=1) — while the one relaxation, test_path_judgments.py:224 from `is` to `issubclass`, slightly loosens what that assertion pins.
justifications.evidence: the done-when's three checks are each recorded — the replay test (head-arm-verified.log 82 passed EXIT=0), the threshold guard, and live-eddb-triage.log STORED judgment_model typesafe/jev-1.13 COMPLETE=1 — and I reproduced the head arm (reviewer-head.log 13 passed) and falsified the threshold guard (reviewer-threshold-guard-red.log 1 failed EXIT=1).
justifications.fit: the try/except with logger.warning(..., exc_info=True) at scorer.py:385 follows the module's logging idiom, the commit subject 'fix(discovery): keep path judgments running after description errors' is conventional with a body, and test_path_scan_threshold.py is named for what it tests with no plan, ticket or phase identifier in the diff.
justifications.goal_fidelity: scorer.py:378 now routes DirectoryTriager.async_triage_batch through the owner describe_paths and scorer.py:385-391 keeps judging on a describe failure, and both describe callers (scorer.py:378, parallel.py:2415) share the one owner.
justifications.reuse: scorer.py:378 deletes its own describe request and calls the existing owner imas_codex/discovery/paths/description.py:36, which parallel.py:2415 already uses, so no capability is forking.
justifications.scope_discipline: git show --stat dac0f8f4 names only the four declared write paths, and the CLI path gate left untouched is explicitly another node's scope per the §14 node-2 comment.
